messages:
alex_support: FYI customer SUP-4321 reported a leaked client secret found in an S3 backup. They pasted it in an internal debug blob. Need rotation + guidance.

maria_security: ack. Can you share minimal repro and whether the key is still active?

alex_support: key is active, last used ~2h ago. bucket path is s3://customer-backups/debug-2026-03-16.tar.gz (we asked them to revoke access already). They want a step-by-step to rotate without downtime.

sam_infra: short plan: 1) create replacement key, 2) update service config to use new key, 3) generate new client credentials, 4) revoke old key, 5) rotate KMS if applicable.

maria_security: also: scope the blast radius. Which privileges did that key have? read-only vs full-admin? Alex, what scope?

alex_support: it was a service key used for uploads and model calls (read+write inference). Customer says it wasn't used for billing ops.

jen_billing: if key touched billing endpoints we need to notify finance. Looks like not. Keep me posted.

maria_security: immediate mitigations: a) restrict key via policy (IP, allowed endpoints) b) enable short-lived token exchange if they can deploy quickly c) rotate as Sam outlined. We should provide CLI/curl snippets.

tim_engineer: snippet to create new API key (internal admin endpoint):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/admin/customers/SUP-4321/keys" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"label":"rotation-march-2026","scopes":["inference:write","inference:read"]}'
```
returns JSON with new_key and key_id. Then update client config to use new_key and verify calls.

alex_support: customer asked if we can purge the leaked secret from their backup object and from our logs.

maria_security: we cannot delete audit logs (retention/compliance), but we can redact secret values from searchable logs and add a metadata note. For S3 object we can advise them to remove the file or replace it and rotate credentials. Provide steps to sanitize.

incident-bot: INCIDENT SUP-4321 created and linked to security response playbook: https://internal.redwood/sop/sec/credential-exposure (assigned to maria_security).

maria_security: legal loop: pinging @legal. We need confirmation on data-retention obligations before promising any irreversible deletions.

legal: quick note — don't promise permanent deletion of audit artifacts. For customer-owned S3 we can advise them to remove the object; for telemetry we can redact or apply retention exemptions after review. Keep records of the request.

sam_infra: post-rotation checklist: - verify no clients still using old key (check last_used) - revoke old key via admin revoke endpoint:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/admin/keys/<OLD_KEY_ID>/revoke" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
- update any KMS alias if they use KMS-wrapped keys: rotate KMS key and re-encrypt persistent secrets.

maria_security: example KMS note to customer: "If you use KMS-wrapped keys, create a new customer-managed KMS key, re-encrypt secrets with the new key, update alias, then schedule deletion of the old CMK once all material has been re-encrypted."

alex_support: customer also wants an SLA-friendly zero-downtime rotation approach. Any patterns?

tim_engineer: run dual-write for a short window: accept both keys for reads, return new tokens for new sessions, expire old tokens after verification. Steps: deploy new key, switch writes to new key, keep old key readable for 5-10 minutes, then cutover and revoke.

maria_security: I'll draft a concise step-by-step and send the playbook link + sample curl commands to the customer. Also ask them to upload a sanitized repro if they need us to confirm the leak path.

alex_support: perfect. I'll send: 1) immediate revoke instructions, 2) rotation curl snippets, 3) KMS guidance, 4) legal note about logs. Ticket SUP-4321 — I'll update when they confirm new key deployed. :thumbsup:
